execution_log.summary: P1 closeout, no change to ttail.sh or to tests 004-006 (git diff --stat empty on all four). NEW: bench.sh (360 lines), tests/007_Bench.sh (360 lines), TEST_COVERAGE_NOTES.md (442 lines). EDITED: README.md (status header -> COMPLETE (P0+P1) with 200/200 per bash; new §9 Performance with a both-bashes table; Tests renumbered to §10 with per-file case counts), PLAN.md (status header -> COMPLETE (P0–P1) + a 'P1 DONE 2026-09-16' block under §4 with the measured table), this ledger, and kcl/README.md (the ttail row in §2, alphabetically after tstringlist, plus the thead row and Twenty -> Twenty-two). bench.sh mirrors thead's shape, with three differences that are this unit's: the (a) runs-nothing proof runs with follow = 1 set, so it also pins that -f reaches the ARGV while three sinks refuse it; (e) zero-fork adds the three follow = 1 refusals (bash-only, no process); and follow is NOT benched at all — tail -f never ends on its own, so nothing about it is a per-call cost, and neither bench.sh nor 007_Bench.sh ever starts a follower. MEASURED on an idle box, GNU coreutils 8.32 — 5.2.37: buildArgv 679.2 us, argv 1282.2 us, new+argv+delete 3202.1 us, bare tail -n 1 35.03 ms vs take 39.13 ms = 1.11x, bare tail -n 5000 33.72 ms vs take 37.57 ms = 1.11x, wc-equivalent 55.60 ms vs t.count 734.09 ms = 13.20x (~135 us/record), gates 2/2 PASS. 5.3.9: 661.9 / 1385.8 / 3333.2 us, 35.08 vs 38.72 ms = 1.10x, 32.56 vs 38.10 ms = 1.17x, 47.26 vs 738.49 ms = 15.62x (~138 us/record), gates 2/2 PASS. Both rc 0 under `bash -eu`. The same two plan estimates as thead are refined (a whole tool run 32-36 ms, not ~42 ms; the wrapper's fixed delta 3.2-3.4 ms, not ~3.9 ms) with the conclusion unchanged. DEVIATION from the letter of the brief: the 007 `count` case runs over 200 records, not the bench's 5000 — the count sink's cost is PER RECORD (~136 us), so at 5000 records the idle ratio is already 13-16x and a 10x ceiling would fail by construction; at 200 records it is under 3x idle and the ceiling still catches an order-of-magnitude regression. GATE: ttail 200/200 on bash 5.2.37 and 200/200 on 5.3.9, threaded, and 200/200 under --mode single on 5.2.37; bash -n clean on bench.sh and 007_Bench.sh; no tests/.tmp left; ps -W before and after shows only the four known phantom cygwin tail.exe rows (PIDs 4204616 4201448 4209672 4212912, 12:39 the previous day) and no follower of ours. P0 implemented red-first against a stubbed skeleton (buildArgv/mapRc/paths/take and the three overridden sinks answering __TTAIL_PENDING__ + rc 2). RED on bash 5.2.37: 189 tests, 44 pass, 145 FAIL (004_Argv 58, 005_Run 51, 006_Contract 34, 2 untagged). GREEN (after one §1.3 behavioural case was added to 005, so 190 tests): 190/190 on bash 5.2.37 and on bash 5.3.9, threaded; 190/190 under --mode single on 5.2.37. Delivered: ttail.sh (TTail : TUtil, sourcing ../tutil/tutil.sh ONLY — never the head wrapper; Create with `parent.constructor tail`; the pinned argv `tail [-q|-v] [-z] [-f] [-n N|-c N] [extras] [-- PATH...]`, so `t.argv V` with follow = 1 still yields -f; the same rc 2 list and the same count regex + 19-digit guard, verbatim; `var follow`; `override func toArray/toList/count` with the rc-preserving spelling `inherited X "$@" || rc=$?; n=$RESULT; kk._return $n; return $rc` and, with follow = 1, one kk.debug line + kk._return '' + return 2 before anything runs; static take), tests/{tests.sh,004_Argv.sh,005_Run.sh,006_Contract.sh}, README.md first cut. T2/T3 pinned: the three refusals with a flag-file producer proving nothing ran and lastRc still -1; `each` + a stopping callback -> rc 0 / lastRc 143 / one record in a child under timeout 20; `first` -> the last line then the stop path; `run` on a growing file delivering the appended line; and, with follow = 0 and a missing operand, all three overrides answering rc 1 with RESULT = the real count (the naive spelling would have answered 0). tail -f hygiene: every follow case runs in a child that ends its own follower (the stop path, or addArg --pid=HELPER for the `run` case), the appender is started by the test with its pid recorded and kill -TERMed in the case's own teardown, and a final case asserts no `tail` process has the test as its parent. `ps -W` before and after the whole phase is byte-identical (16 foreign followers from earlier sessions, none of ours). DEVIATION: the growing-file case first used a fixed `sleep 2` for the appender and flaked — a cold `source` of the unit costs seconds under the 8-worker runner, so the append landed BEFORE tail started and `tail -n 1` printed only the appended line; replaced by a bounded READY-flag handshake (the child touches the flag immediately before `run`, the appender then waits 1 s), which keeps >= 3 s of slack before the --pid helper ends the follow. REVIEW (supervisor, 2026-09-16): ttail suite reproduced on both bashes (thead 173/173, ttail 190/190; tutil 187/187 after the _badOut extension); probes on both bashes — argv shape, -0/+0 sign table (head -0 = 5 records, tail +2 = 4, tail -0 = 0), 1K and lines+bytes rc 2, __th_ out-name refused, crlf=1 strips the CR, take one-liners, follow: count rc 2 and each+stop rc 0/lastRc 143, partial failure keeps records with rc 1. The worker's two plan corrections (8 records for the unterminated pair; overflow rc 1 only for -c -N) accepted and written into thead PLAN §2.4/§2.5/H3/H7/§8. Master sweep 25/25 suites 0 [FAIL] on 5.3.9; on 5.2.37 the first run had ONE unrelated FAIL (dateutils 001 now()-nowUTC(): two separate samplings with 1 s slack drifted 1.5 s under the loaded first suite — a pre-existing dateutils test flake, open item), the rerun 25/25 0 [FAIL]. Four phantom cygwin `tail.exe` rows in `ps -W` from the critic's probes cannot be killed (cygwin kill: no such process; PowerShell cannot see them) — process-table ghosts, not processes.
